title: Bryophyta — Liverworts, Hornworts and Mosses
topicTitle: Bryophyta: General introduction and characteristic features of liverworts, hornworts and moss; morphological structure and reproduction of Marchantia; economic importance of bryophytes
notes: **General features:** non-vascular plants, dominant gametophyte, sporophyte dependent on gametophyte, require water for fertilisation, called amphibians of plant kingdom.

**Hepaticopsida (liverworts):** thalloid body, dorsiventral, rhizoids unicellular. Example: Marchantia has umbrella-shaped archegoniophores and antheridiophores. Asexual reproduction by gemmae in gemma cups.
**Anthocerotopsida (hornworts):** elongated horn-like sporophyte, photosynthetic, thick walled spores with pseudo-elaters.
**Bryopsida (mosses):** leafy gametophyte, multicellular rhizoids, peristome teeth for spore release. Example: Funaria. Protonema stage (filamentous) precedes gametophyte.
**Economic importance:** peat formation (Sphagnum used as fuel and packing material), soil formation and erosion control, water retention in forests, indicator of pollution.
